title: Shallow-Reef Sampling Log
premise: A long reef-diving drama spanning years. Langlang and Achao are easily confused; the coral sample case goes intact→seal ruptured→resealed repair; the fiberglass skiff is wrecked and sunk and must be avoided; count memory (ship lanterns / dive buoy flags / fog-navigation brass bells), false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_diver: A reef diver in his forties named Haisheng, buzz-cut hair, navy wetsuit, silver tank on his shoulder, sharp eyes.
states.ear_injury: The same diver after injury: right ear wrapped in gauze, limping, wetsuit shoulder strap broken and tied with rope.
states.deceased: Haisheng has passed peacefully, eyes closed on the dock planks, face serene, breath gone.

states.adult_successor: Adult Langlang: a broad-shouldered steady young diver in his twenties, still in orange-yellow headscarf, now carrying twin tanks.

states.seal_ruptured: The same sample case with a torn gasket letting in seawater, compartments askew, brass handle bent.
states.resealed_repair: The sample case fitted with a new gasket, handle straightened, compartments reset—ready for diving again.

segments.action: At dusk, Haisheng dives from the dock into the shallow reef coral zone and checks tank pressure.
A row of five ship lanterns hangs on the dock supply hut wall; Haisheng comes ashore and polishes them one by one.
Two fog-navigation brass bells hang under the dock eaves; Haisheng reaches up and lets them ring softly.
Haisheng sets the coral sample case on a surface float and checks the gasket seal.
Haisheng surfaces and gazes at the darkening reef line.
The coral sample case gleams transparent in clear seawater, compartments sharp.
Haisheng sits on the dock planks, listening to waves on the reef.
In the dock supply hut, Haisheng opens the dive log and records depth and visibility.
Haisheng sketches today's sampling points on a blank page.
Haisheng closes the dive log and slips it into a waterproof bag.
Brass handle light from the coral sample case sweeps across Haisheng's cheek.
At dawn on the dock, Haisheng greets young Langlang arriving in the fiberglass skiff.
Langlang jumps off the fiberglass skiff and hangs the orange life ring back on the gunwale.
Haisheng points to three dive buoy flags stuck in the floats and teaches Langlang flag signals.
Langlang crouches by the wooden walkway, curious, touching wet mooring rope.
Haisheng explains shallow reef currents and no-dive zones to Langlang.
Langlang looks back at the intact fiberglass skiff, eyes full of longing.
Behind a fish stall at the fishing village dock market, green-headscarfed Achao glances back.

segments.action: The coral sample case stands transparent under the ship lanterns.
Dry season clarity—day after day Haisheng dives the shallow reef coral zone.
Another pre-typhoon night, Haisheng checks tank valves.
Rainy season murk—Haisheng sorts buoys at the dock.
Midsummer noon, Haisheng wipes sun-hot brass handles.
Autumn swell—Haisheng keeps lone watch until dawn.
Another new-year dive—Haisheng recalibrates his dive computer.
Clear sunny day—Haisheng photographs new staghorn coral shoots.
At dawn, Haisheng patrols the dock; the fiberglass skiff moored at the pier.
Haisheng crouches to inspect the fiberglass skiff's keel guard strip.
Haisheng walks to the floats—those three dive buoy flags still in place.
An unfamiliar gray motorboat passes the harbor, wider hull—not the fiberglass skiff.
Haisheng stands on the walkway, recording exposed reef after low tide.
Haisheng hangs wetsuits on the dock supply hut wooden rack.
Storm rises; shallow reef walls of water surge; the coral sample case jolts violently.
Lightning lights the reef line; seawater turns gray-white.
A huge wave hits; the coral sample case gasket tears and seawater floods in, brass handle bent.

segments.action: An orange-black rented rubber dinghy enters the harbor—nothing like the long-wrecked fiberglass skiff.
A coast guard patrol officer jumps onto the dock and talks beside Haisheng, builds alike.
The coast guard patrol officer points at the rented rubber dinghy, explaining temporary closure orders.
The rented rubber dinghy departs; Haisheng alone on the dock watching it go.
At the fishing village dock market, a light-brown-headscarfed traveling diver girl arrives—at a glance somewhat like young Langlang.
The traveling diver girl tries shouldering a small tank; Haisheng shakes his head—she is not Langlang after all.
Years later at dusk, Haisheng stands limping on the abandoned lighthouse reef, right ear wrapped in gauze.
